root_causes: The original BG169 workflow hard-coded merge_method=merge although the actual protected GitHub repository disables merge commits and permits squash only.
After a squash the original feature head is not an ancestor of main: naive git merge-base --is-ancestor candidate_sha origin/main would mislabel a valid squash as failed.
BG169 previously could pass every quality gate yet remain permanently unable to promote any future candidate.
fix: Select the existing GitHub policy-approved squash method and fail closed when allow_squash_merge is false; leave GitHub protection unchanged.
Preserve immutable sha=$HEAD_SHA compare-and-swap plus zero-behind, main-epoch and terminal duplicate guards.

After provider accepted squash merge, verify returned merge SHA, source tree equality, first parent exactly equal original rollback/main epoch, resulting merge commit ancestor of current protected main, and GitHub PR merged with exact provider SHA.
Store canonical BG169 evidence with merge_method, merge_commit_sha and verified_candidate_tree; do not claim Netlify/publication from GitHub transport alone.
prevention: Never assume a repository allows merge commits; use current repository settings before a native protected release.
SQUASH lineage must be proven through exact source tree and first parent, not feature-head ancestry.
Original BRAIN-delivery tests explicitly reject disallowed merge method, missing source-tree verification or any bypass to Make; production provider readback remains independent.
